evidence: Frozen workbook Quality Checks!C44:D44 requires gates before shaping with no reward mass and a functional floor; Internal Quality Checks!D44 says failed gates hard-zero and cheap gates alone earn little. Candidate tests/scoring.toml:1-11 exactly matches the frozen template: render=constraints=0.0, weights functional/polish/visual=0.6/0.2/0.2, functional floor=0.05. Both gate judge.toml files specify aggregation=all_pass and one binary criterion. Candidate tests/test.sh:212-227 removes prior scored output, runs gates, invokes score.py, exits on gate status 1, and only then runs scored; its initial zero reward and trap are at lines 7-20 and 60-61. Candidate tests/tools/score.py:31-58 excludes gate values from the weighted sum and returns zero unless gates and functional floor pass. Independent synthetic invocation of the frozen score.py (per-row-review/evidence/43/scorer-probes.json) produced reward=0 and exit=1 for either failed gate despite all scored values=1; reward=0 for functional=0 or exactly 0.05 with polish=visual=1; reward=0.6 for functional=1 with no craft. A plausible polished minimal app with a working JS Run and server-backed save/readback could clear the gates while missing most other product behavior; synthetic functional=0.06 plus perfect craft yields 0.436, an above-floor partial-app boundary rather than a dead-app pass. I also checked the conforming server-rendered storage alternative: constraints/judge.toml explicitly accepts server-rendered records and forbids requiring a JSON/list endpoint, so this gate does not reject that implementation by format alone. Frozen candidate/template files and cited raw gate artifacts match their manifest/index SHA256. The raw mock gate observation rejects a literal-string fake and old Luna observation passes computed output, but these are scripted browser checks, not RewardKit gate or full judge runs. No runtime-evidence.json or full configured judge record exists, so end-to-end gating and score behavior remain unmeasured and risk stays true.
